Rashi on Sanhedrin 8b:1:1.hebrew: וחכ"א תבעו ממון כו' - ברייתא היא:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 8b:1:1.english: And the Rabbis say: [If] they claimed money, etc. - It is a baraita.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 8b:1:2.hebrew: תבעו ממון תחילה - דלא בא לידון בעדים אלא על פיו, ולהפסידה כתובתה — מודינן דבשלשה:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 8b:1:2.english: [If] he claimed money at the outset - Where he did not come to litigate with witnesses, but rather based on his [own] word, and [merely] to cause her to forfeit her marriage contract — we agree that [it is judged] by three [judges].

Rashi on Sanhedrin 8b:1:3.english: [If] he initially claimed capital punishment - Where he said [that he would] bring witnesses.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 8b:1:4.hebrew: אפילו ממון - כגון אם לא מצא עדים, ואמר: "דונו לי מיהא להפסידה כתובה", אעפ"כ בעינן עשרים ושלשה משום כבוד ראשונים:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 8b:1:4.english: Even a monetary [claim] - For example, if he did not find witnesses, and said: "Judge for me at least to cause her to forfeit [her] ketubah," nevertheless we require twenty-three [judges] because of the honor of the first [judges].

Rashi on Sanhedrin 8b:1:5.hebrew: אלא לעולא - דאמר: רבנן ללעז חיישי, שמא ישמעו עדים ויבואו — "תבעו ממון בשלשה" היכי משכחת לה? לעולם עשרים ושלשה לרבנן בעינן, משום דחוששין ללעז:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 8b:1:5.english: But according to Ulla - For he said [that] the Rabbis are concerned about rumor, lest witnesses hear and come [forward] — how can you find [a case where] “he claimed money [and it is judged] by three”? According to the Rabbis, we should always require twenty-three, because they are concerned about rumor.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 8b:2:1.hebrew: והזימום - דתו ליכא למיחש ללעז, דאיגלי מילתא דאהני סהדי סמיך, והני סהדי שקרי נינהו. ואפילו להפסידה כתובתה לא מהימני, דהשתא בתר סהדי שקרי קא מהדר ושקורי קמשקר, ובעי למיתב מאה סלע לאב ולו תהיה לאשה. ותבעו ממון דקאמרי רבנן — אתביעת מאה סלע שהאב תובע קאי. והכי קאמר: בא האב לגבות ממון מבעל שנמצא כבר שקרן — בשלשה, דהזמנה אחריתי היא. ואפילו כבוד ראשונים ליכא למימר הכא, דדינא אחרינא הוא, דמעיקרא בעל הוה תובע, והשתא אב קא תבע:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 8b:2:1.english: And they rendered them conspiring witnesses - For there is no longer any reason to be concerned about a rumor, since the matter has been revealed that he was relying on these witnesses, and these witnesses are liars. And even to cause her to forfeit her ketubah they are not believed, since now [it is apparent that] he seeks out false witnesses and is telling lies, and he must give one hundred sela to the father, and “she shall be his wife.” And “claimed money,” which the Rabbis stated, refers to the claim of the one hundred sela that the father claims. And this is what it means: [If] the father comes to collect money from the husband, who was already found to be a liar — [this is adjudicated] by three [judges], for it is a different summons. And even [the concern for] the honor of the first [judges] cannot be said here, because it is a different lawsuit, for initially the husband was the claimant, and now the father is claiming:

Rashi on Sanhedrin 8b:2:2.hebrew: ובמקום דאיכא דיני נפשות - כלומר: וכל היכא דאיכא למיחש לנפשות — כגון בתחילת הדין, אפילו אין לו עדים, יש לחוש שמא ישמעו ויבואו עדים — עשרים ושלשה בעי. ואית דמפרשי כל תביעת ממון דהא שמעתתא — אמאה כסף דאב תבע לבעל. ואי אפשר לומר כן: דהא לא מחייב בעל מאה סלעים אא"כ הביא עדים והוזמו, דכל זמן שלא הביא עדים נאמן אף להפסידה כתובה, כדפרישית לעיל; ואי בשהוזמו עדיו מיירי מתניתין, תו ליכא למימר חוששין ללעז. ועוד, מדגרסינן בתירוצא דרב חייא בר אבין: "בא לגבות ממון מבעל", דפריש דרבי חייא להאי "תבעו ממון" אמאה סלע — מכלל דעד השתא הוה שמעינן "תבעו ממון" אבעל, ואיהו תבע להפסיד כתובה:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 8b:2:2.english: And in a case where there is capital law - That is to say: And wherever there is [reason] to be concerned for capital punishment — such as at the beginning of the case, [where] even if he has no witnesses, there is [reason] to be concerned lest witnesses hear and come [forward] — it requires twenty-three [judges]. And there are those who explain every monetary claim in this sugya as [referring to] the hundred [pieces of] silver that the father claims from the husband. And it is impossible to say so, for the husband is not liable for one hundred selas unless he brought witnesses and they were rendered conspiring [witnesses], for as long as he has not brought witnesses, he is believed even to cause her to forfeit [her] ketubah, as I explained above; and if the Mishnah is dealing with [a case] where his witnesses were rendered conspiring, one can no longer say that we are concerned about rumors. And furthermore, from [the fact] that we have the textual reading in the resolution of Rav Ḥiyya bar Avin: "If he comes to collect money from the husband", [showing] that Rav Ḥiyya explained this [clause] "they claimed money" as [referring to] the hundred selas, it follows by implication that until now we understood "they claimed money" [as referring to] the husband, and [that] he was claiming to cause [her] to forfeit [her] ketubah.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 8b:3:1.hebrew: אביי אמר - אי בשלא הביא עדים, דכולי עלמא חוששין ללעז ובעינן עשרים ושלשה — דילמא שמעי סהדי ואתו; ומדבעינן עשרים ושלשה ברישא, אפילו ממון בעשרים ושלשה, דחוששין לכבודן של ראשונים. והכא בפלוגתא דמתניתין — כגון שהביא עדים בתחילת הזמנתו לדין, דתו ליכא למיחש סהדי אחריני; והני אמרי באפי תלתא דהתרו בה מיתה סתם, ולא הזכירו לה סקילה כדין נערה המאורסה. רבי מאיר סבר: תו ליכא הכא דיני נפשות, ובהני שלשה סגי למידן דיני ממונות דכתובה, דכי נמי יוזמו ישלם מאה כסף. ורבנן סברי: כיון דאתרו ביה מיתה, דיני נפשות איכא, ומיקטלא. והאי תנא הוא, וכו'. וברייתא דקתני לרבנן תבעו ממון בשלשה — כדתרצה רב חייא בר אבין:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 8b:3:1.english: Abaye said - If [the case was] where he did not bring witnesses, everyone agrees that we are concerned for rumors, and we require twenty-three [judges] — lest witnesses hear and come; and since we require twenty-three at the beginning, even [for the subsequent claim of] money, [it is judged] by twenty-three, for we are concerned for the honor of the first [judges]. And here, regarding the dispute of our Mishnah, [it is a case] where he brought witnesses at the start of his summons to court, so that there is no longer any concern for other witnesses; and these [witnesses] said before three [judges] that they had warned her of the death penalty without specification, and did not mention stoning to her in accordance with the law of a betrothed maiden. Rabbi Meir holds: There is no longer a capital case here, and with these three [judges] it is sufficient to adjudicate the monetary law of the marriage contract, for even if they are proven to be conspiring witnesses, he [the husband] will pay one hundred [shekels of] silver. And the Rabbis hold: Since they warned her of death, there is a capital case, and she is executed. [And this explains the Gemara's statement:] "And it is this Tanna, etc." And the baraita which teaches according to the Rabbis, "[If] they claimed money, [it is adjudicated] by three" — [is explained] as Rav Ḥiyya bar Avin resolved it:

Rashi on Sanhedrin 8b:4:1.hebrew: ושאר כל חייבי מיתות כו' - גבי מסית קאי, דרחמנא אמר (דברים י״ג:ט׳): "לא תחמול ולא תכסה", ונהרג בלי התראה על ידי הכמנת עדים:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 8b:4:1.english: And all other people liable to death penalties, etc. - [This] refers to an inciter [to idolatry], as the Merciful One stated: (Deuteronomy 13:9) "Neither shall you spare, neither shall you conceal him"; and he is executed without forewarning, by means of concealing witnesses.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 8b:4:3.hebrew: ועד שיודיעוהו - עדיו בשעת התראה, שהוא חייב מיתה בבית דין אם יעבור עבירה זו. ומיהו, אע"ג דלא מזכרי ליה איזו מיתה, התראה היא ומחייב — כרבנן:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 8b:4:3.english: And until they inform him - His witnesses [must inform him] at the time of forewarning that he is liable to the death penalty by the court if he commits this transgression. However, even though they do not specify to him which death [penalty], it is [a valid] forewarning and he is liable, in accordance with the Rabbis.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 8b:6:1.hebrew: רב פפא - כדאביי נמי סבירא ליה, דחוששין ללעז ולכבודן של ראשונים. והכא, דאמר רבי מאיר בג' — כגון שהביא עדים עמו בתחלת הזמנתו לדין, ואמרו שלא התרו בה, לפי שהאשה חבירה היא ולא הוצרכנו להתרות בה. רבי מאיר סבר: אף על גב דחבירה היא — לא מיקטלא; הלכך, לא צריכין לאיכנופי תו עשרים ושלשה, אלא שלשה לדון דיני ממונות דכתובה. ורבנן סברי כרבי יוסי בר' יהודה:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 8b:6:1.english: Rav Pappa - He also holds in accordance with Abaye, that we are concerned for rumors and for the honor of the initial [judges]. And here, where Rabbi Meir said [the case is judged] by three [judges — it is a case] such as where he brought witnesses with him at the beginning of his summons to court, and they said that they did not forewarn her, because the woman is a ḥaveira and [therefore,] "We did not need to forewarn her." Rabbi Meir holds: Even though she is a ḥaveira, she is not executed [without forewarning]; therefore, they do not need to assemble twenty-three [judges] further, but rather three [suffice] to judge the monetary laws of the ketubah. And the Rabbis hold in accordance with Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 8b:6:2.english: Only to distinguish - So that he cannot say, “I thought that [it was] permitted.”

Tosafot on Sanhedrin 8b:1:1.hebrew: מיתיבי כו' בשלמא לרבה תבעו ממון תחלה - כלומר, דלא איכניף לדיני נפשות:
Tosafot on Sanhedrin 8b:1:1.english: "They raised an objection, etc. Granted, according to Rabbah, [if] he claimed money initially" - That is to say, that [a court] was not assembled for capital cases.

Tosafot on Sanhedrin 8b:2:1.hebrew: והביא האב עדים והזימום - קודם גמר הדין, דהשתא ליכא מיתה בזוממין, בא לגבות ממון — בג', דליכא למיחש ללעז שמא יבואו עדים אחרים ויצטרכו להוסיף, דכיון דהוזמו ודאי סהדי שקרי נינהו. ובמקום דאיכא נפשות, כלומר שיכול לבא לידי נפשות שלא הוזמו אלא הוכחשו — בעי כ"ג. ותבעו נפשות — ה"פ: תבעו ממון שיכול לבא לידי נפשות. וניחא לפירוש רבינו תם הא דאיצטריך לאביי למימר: דכ"ע חוששין ללעז, דכולה סוגיא איירי כשהוכחשו עדי הבעל או לא כוונו עדותן, ומשום דחוששין ללעז הוי בכ"ג לרבנן, דאיכא חששא דלעז דשייכא מיתה בהתראה סתם דשמא יצטרכו להוסיף; אבל לפירוש הקונטרס, הכי נמי הוה מצי למימר: דכ"ע אין חוששין ללעז, אפ"ה הוי לרבנן בעשרים ושלשה. וי"מ לפי' הקונטרס: דלהכי נקט דכ"ע חוששין ללעז משום רבותא דר' מאיר, דאע"ג דחוששין ללעז, הוי לר' מאיר בשלשה, כיון דליכא למיחש לסהדי אחריני. ומיהו קשה לפר"ת למאי דמסיק: פלוגתא דמתניתין בפלוגתא דבן זכאי — דהשתא מוציא שם רע דרבי מאיר דאמר בשלשה, הוי תביעת מאה כסף דקתבע אב, ומוציא שם רע בעשרים ושלשה דרבנן, היינו בחיוב מיתת האשה, ולא בתביעת ממון, דאין עדותן בטלה בהכחשת בדיק' לרבנן. ועוד, דמשמע דקאי אהא דאמר: דכולי עלמא חוששין ללעז; ואי חוששין ללעז, כי איתכחוש נמי ליהוי בכ"ג לרבי מאיר, שמא יבואו עדים אחרים ויצטרכו להוסיף ויהיה לעז! ומיהו יש ליישב, כדמוקי: כגון דאיתכחיש בבדיקות, איירי נמי שהכחישו אח"כ עדי האב הכחשה גמורה, דהשתא לא מקטלא נמי לרבנן, ואפ"ה הוו בכ"ג, דאיכא למיחש לסהדי אחריני; ואע"ג דהני אחריני נמי יהיו מוכחשין בבדיקות, מ"מ מיקטלא לרבנן, דהכחשה דבדיקות לאו הכחשה היא, ולר"מ הוה הכחשה. ואין להקשות לפר"ת לאביי ולכולהו אמוראי דלקמן: דלא מיחייב מיתה לר"מ, היכי מיחייב ק' כסף? הא קיי"ל בכתובות דלא מיחייב ק' סלע היכא דלא מצי למיתי לידי חיוב סקילה, דאמר בפרק נערה (כתובות דף מד:): המוציא שם רע על הקטנה פטור, כיון דלא מצי למיקיימא "אם אמת היה הדבר" וסקלו? ויש לומר: דמהאי טעמא לא ממעטינן אלא קטנה, דלאו בת עונשין כלל. אבל נראה דוחק מה שפירש ר"ת, דהכחשה בלא הזמה מחייב ק' סלעים. וצ"ל לפר"ת שהיא מותרת לבעלה כשלא כוונו עדותן או כשהוכחשו, דאי לאו הכי, היכי מחייב ק' סלעים? הא לא קרינן ביה (דברים כ״ב:י״ט) "ולו תהיה לאשה"! ויש ללמוד מכאן, דאי אתו עדים ואמרו: "אשת פלוני זנתה", דבעי דרישה וחקירה לאוסרה על בעלה; וסברא הוא, דלא גרע מגזלות וחבלות. ובירושלמי מצא רשב"א פלוגתא דאמוראי, דאיכא דמפרש פלוגתא לענין כתובה כדמפרש בקונטרס, ואיכא דמפרש לענין ק' סלע כדמפרש רבינו תם:
Tosafot on Sanhedrin 8b:2:1.english: "And the father brought witnesses and they proved them to be conspiring witnesses" - [This occurred] before the verdict, when now there is no death penalty for the conspiring witnesses; [if the father] comes to collect money, [it is adjudicated] by three [judges], for there is no concern about casting aspersion lest other witnesses come and they need to add [judges to make twenty-three], since once they were proved to be conspiring witnesses, they are certainly lying witnesses. And where there are capital consequences — that is to say, that it could lead to capital consequences, where they were not proved to be conspiring witnesses but rather were contradicted — it requires twenty-three [judges]. And [when the baraita states:] "They claimed a capital case" — this is what it means: They claimed money that could lead to a capital case. And this works out well according to the interpretation of Rabbeinu Tam as to why Abaye needed to say: "Everyone is concerned about casting aspersion," for the entire sugya is dealing with a case where the husband's witnesses were contradicted or did not align their testimony, and because we are concerned about casting aspersion, it is [judged] by twenty-three according to the Rabbis; for there is a concern of aspersion that the death penalty is applicable with an unspecified warning, lest they need to add [judges]. But according to the interpretation of the Kuntres [Rashi], he could just as well have said: "Everyone is not concerned about casting aspersion," and even so it would be [judged] by twenty-three according to the Rabbis. And some explain in defense of the interpretation of the Kuntres: that [Abaye] stated that everyone is concerned about casting aspersion due to the novelty of Rabbi Meir's view — that even though we are concerned about casting aspersion, according to Rabbi Meir it is [judged] by three, since there is no concern for other witnesses [coming]. However, there is a difficulty according to the interpretation of Rabbeinu Tam regarding that which [the Gemara] concludes: that the dispute in our Mishnah is the same as the dispute of Ben Zakkai — for now, [the case of] a defamer according to Rabbi Meir, who said [it is judged] by three, is the claim of the one hundred [pieces of] silver that the father claims, and [the case of] a defamer [judged] by twenty-three according to the Rabbis is regarding the liability of the death penalty of the woman, and not regarding the monetary claim, since their testimony is not voided by contradiction during cross-examination according to the Rabbis. Furthermore, it implies that it is based on that which [Abaye] said, that everyone is concerned about casting aspersion; and if we are concerned about casting aspersion, when they were contradicted, let it also be [judged] by twenty-three according to Rabbi Meir, lest other witnesses come and they need to add [judges], and there will be aspersion! However, this can be resolved: as it establishes [the case], such as where they were contradicted in the cross-examinations, it is also dealing with a case where the father's witnesses subsequently contradicted them with a complete contradiction, so that now she is also not executed according to the Rabbis, and even so it was [judged] by twenty-three, because there is concern for other witnesses [coming]; and even though these other [witnesses] would also be contradicted in the cross-examinations, nevertheless she would be executed according to the Rabbis, since contradiction in cross-examinations is not considered a contradiction [according to the Rabbis], whereas according to Rabbi Meir it was considered a contradiction. And one should not raise a difficulty against the interpretation of Rabbeinu Tam, against Abaye and all the Amoraim below: Since she is not liable to the death penalty according to Rabbi Meir, how can [the husband] be liable to the one hundred [pieces of] silver? For don't we maintain in Ketubot that one is not liable to the one hundred sela where it could not have led to liability of stoning, as [the Gemara] says in the chapter [entitled] Na'arah (Ketubot 44b): "One who defames a minor girl is exempt, since it cannot be fulfilled: 'If the matter was true...' and they stone [her]"? And one can say: It is only a minor girl who is excluded for this reason, since she is not subject to punishment at all. However, what Rabbeinu Tam explained seems forced — that contradiction without hazamah obligates [payment of] the one hundred sela. And one must say according to the interpretation of Rabbeinu Tam that she is permitted to her husband when they did not align their testimony or when they were contradicted, for if that were not so, how could he be liable to the one hundred sela? For [in that case] we would not read regarding him (Deuteronomy 22:19): "And she shall be his wife"! And one can learn from here that if witnesses come and say, "So-and-so's wife committed adultery," it requires interrogation and inquiry to forbid her to her husband; and this stands to reason, as it is no worse than [cases of] robbery and personal injury. And in the Yerushalmi, the Rashba [Rabbeinu Shimshon of Sens] found a dispute of Amoraim, where there is one who explains the dispute regarding the marriage contract, as explained in the Kuntres, and there is one who explains [it] regarding the one hundred sela, as Rabbeinu Tam explains.

Tosafot on Sanhedrin 8b:3:1.hebrew: חוששין ללעז וחוששין לכבודן של ראשונים - אע"ג דחוששין ללעז, אכתי נפקא לן במאי דחוששין לכבודן של ראשונים: שהביא הבעל עדים שזינתה, והביא האב עדים והזימום. וה"ה דהוה מצי למימר: "אין חוששין לכבודן של ראשונים". אבל אין לפרש: מדחוששין ללעז כ"ש דחוששין לכבוד של ראשונים, כדמוכח מדרבא — חדא, מה ענין זה אצל זה? ועוד, דהא לעולא דחוששין רבנן ללעז, ולכבודן של ראשונים לא חיישינן, דהיכא דהבעל הביא עדים והביא האב עדים והזימום, אמרי רבנן: בא לגבות ממון בג'. וא"ת: אביי ושאר אמוראי דלקמן היכי מוקמי "שתבעו ממון בשלשה"? דלדידהו ליכא לאוקמי כגון שהביא הבעל עדים שזינתה והביא האב עדים והזימום כדמוקי לעיל, כיון דסברי רבנן דכולי עלמא חוששין לכבודן של ראשונים! ויש לומר: דלדידהו "תבעו ממון" היינו שלא התרו בה כלל, דליכא מיתה אלא ממון. ובקונטרס פירש: דמוקי לה כרבא ורבי חייא, שהביא הבעל עדים שזינתה והאב הביא עדים והזימום, וליכא למיחש לכבודם של ראשונים, דדינא אחרינא הוא, דמעיקרא הוה בעל תובע. ונראה דוחק:
Tosafot on Sanhedrin 8b:3:1.english: "[One is] concerned for rumors and [one is] concerned for the honor of the first [judges]" - Even though [everyone agrees that] we are concerned for rumors, there is still a practical difference for us in [holding] that we are concerned for the honor of the first [judges]: [in a case] where the husband brought witnesses that she committed adultery, and the father brought witnesses and rendered them zomemim. And by the same token, he could have said: "[Everyone agrees that] we are not concerned for the honor of the first [judges]." But one cannot explain that since one is concerned for rumors, all the more so one is concerned for the honor of the first [judges] — as might seem proven from Rava — for one [reason]: what does one matter have to do with the other? And furthermore: according to Ulla, the Rabbis are concerned for rumors, yet we are not concerned for the honor of the first [judges], for where the husband brought witnesses and the father brought witnesses and rendered them zomemim, the Rabbis say: [if he] comes to collect money, [it is adjudicated] by three [judges]. And if you should ask: How do Abaye and the other Amoraim below establish [the statement that] "if they claimed money, [it is adjudicated] by three"? For according to them, it cannot be established as [referring to a case] where the husband brought witnesses that she committed adultery and the father brought witnesses and rendered them zomemim, as [Rava] established above, since the Rabbis hold that everyone is concerned for the honor of the first [judges]! And one can answer: According to them, "they claimed money" means that they did not forewarn her at all, so that there is no death penalty, only money. And in the Kunteres [Rashi] explained that [Abaye] establishes it in accordance with Rava and Rabbi Ḥiyya, where the husband brought witnesses that she committed adultery and the father brought witnesses and rendered them zomemim, and there is no reason to be concerned for the honor of the first [judges], because it is a different case, since initially the husband was the claimant. But this appears forced.

Tosafot on Sanhedrin 8b:4:1.hebrew: בעדה ועדים ובהתראה - ומסית נמי צריך עדה; אלא משום דכתיב (במדבר ל״ה:כ״ה): "והצילו העדה", ומסית אין מהפכין בזכותו, שאין טוענין למסית. אבל לענין עשרים ושלשה — דרשינן מהאי קרא, דאין סברא לחלק בין מסית לשאר חייבי מיתות. ועדים והתראה נמי צריך במסית; אלא משום שמכמינין לו עדים, וגם אין מתרין בו בפירוש, אלא אומרים לו: "היאך נניח אבינו שבשמים ונעבוד עצים ואבנים?", כדתניא פרק ד' מיתות (לקמן סנהדרין דף סז.):
Tosafot on Sanhedrin 8b:4:1.english: "With a congregation, and witnesses, and with forewarning" - And an inciter [to idol worship] also requires a congregation [i.e., a court of twenty-three judges]; rather, [the baraita states this] because it is written: "And the congregation shall save [the slayer]" (Numbers 35:25), and for an inciter one does not search for grounds for his acquittal, as one does not plead [arguments in favor of] an inciter. But regarding [the requirement of] twenty-three [judges], we derive [it] from this verse, for there is no reason to differentiate between an inciter and other offenders liable to the death penalty. And witnesses and forewarning are also required for an inciter; rather, [the baraita mentions them] because witnesses are hidden in ambush for him, and also they do not forewarn him explicitly, but rather they say to him: "How shall we forsake our Father in Heaven and worship wood and stone?", as it is taught in the chapter [entitled] Arba Mitot (below, Sanhedrin 67a).

Tosafot on Sanhedrin 8b:6:1.hebrew: באשה חבירה - וכגון דאמר שבעל וחזר ובעל, דאי לאו הכי — מתוך שאין נהרגין, שיכולין לומר: "לאוסרה על בעלה באנו", אף היא אינה נהרגת, כדאמרינן בריש היו בודקין (לקמן סנהדרין דף מא.):
Tosafot on Sanhedrin 8b:6:1.english: With a woman who is a ḥaveira - And [this is] for example where [the witness] says that [the paramour] had intercourse and had intercourse again. For if not so, since [the witnesses] are not executed — as they can say, "We came to forbid her to her husband" — she too is not executed, as we say at the beginning of Hayu Vodekin (below, Sanhedrin 41a).
